title: X-Men
note: The first Fox X-Men film, with Patrick Stewart as Professor X and Ian McKellen as Magneto.

links.text: Patrick Stewart’s Professor X appears in Multiverse of Madness.
Stewart, McKellen, James Marsden and Rebecca Romijn are in the Doomsday cast.

title: Spider-Man
note: Tobey Maguire’s Peter Parker vs. the Green Goblin, in Sam Raimi’s first Spider-Man film.

links.text: Maguire’s Peter and Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin return in No Way Home.

title: X2: X-Men United
note: Introduces Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming) and pits the X-Men against William Stryker.

links.text: Cumming’s Nightcrawler is in the Doomsday cast.

title: Spider-Man 2
note: Peter takes on Doctor Octopus.

links.text: Alfred Molina’s Doc Ock returns in No Way Home.

title: X-Men: The Last Stand
note: Introduces Beast (Kelsey Grammer) and plays out the Dark Phoenix storyline.

links.text: Grammer’s Beast appears in The Marvels’ mid-credits scene.
Grammer is in the Doomsday cast.

title: Spider-Man 3
note: Peter faces Sandman, the symbiote and Harry Osborn.

links.text: Thomas Haden Church’s Sandman returns in No Way Home.

title: Iron Man
note: Tony Stark builds the first suit. Post-credits scene: {{Nick Fury pitches the Avengers Initiative.}}

links.text: Fury’s pitch becomes the team-up film.

title: The Incredible Hulk
note: Introduces Thaddeus Ross, Emil Blonsky and Samuel Sterns. {{Tony Stark appears in the final scene.}}

links.text: Sterns’s tease pays off 17 years later as the Leader, and Ross becomes Red Hulk.
Blonsky returns as Abomination, out of prison.
Abomination turns up in the Macau fight club.

title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
note: Wolverine’s origin story, with Ryan Reynolds as a version of Wade Wilson.

title: Iron Man 2
note: Introduces Black Widow and gives Rhodey the War Machine armor. Post-credits scene: {{Coulson finds a crater in New Mexico.}}

links.text: The New Mexico crater is where Thor lands.

title: Marvel One-Shot: The Consultant
releaseNote: Released later, on Sep 13, 2011, on the Thor home video.
note: A two-hander with Agent Coulson and Jasper Sitwell, set around the events of The Incredible Hulk.

links.text: It runs alongside the Tony Stark scene that closes The Incredible Hulk.

title: Marvel One-Shot: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Thor’s Hammer
releaseNote: Released later, on Oct 25, 2011, on the Captain America: The First Avenger home video.
note: Agent Coulson stops at a convenience store on his way to New Mexico and ends up in a robbery.

links.text: Coulson’s drive is toward the New Mexico site from Thor.

title: Thor
note: Thor is banished to Earth. Loki’s scheming and the Tesseract carry straight into the Avengers.

links.text: Loki returns as the main villain.

title: X-Men: First Class
note: A young Charles Xavier and Erik Lehnsherr form the X-Men in 1962.

title: Captain America: The First Avenger
note: Steve Rogers, Bucky, Peggy Carter, the Red Skull and Hydra in the 1940s.

links.text: Hydra’s survival and Bucky’s fate come back.

title: Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter
releaseNote: Released later, on Sep 3, 2013, on the Iron Man 3 home video.
note: Peggy Carter works for the Strategic Scientific Reserve about a year after the war.

links.text: It led to the Agent Carter TV series.

title: The Avengers
note: Six heroes unite against Loki and the Chitauri. Mid-credits scene: {{Thanos appears.}}

links.text: Thanos’s first on-screen glimpse, six years early.

title: Marvel One-Shot: Item 47
releaseNote: Released later, on Sep 25, 2012, on The Avengers home video.
note: A couple finds a discarded Chitauri weapon after the Battle of New York.

links.text: It helped inspire Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
note: Andrew Garfield’s Peter faces the Lizard (Rhys Ifans).

links.text: Garfield’s Peter and Rhys Ifans’s Lizard return in No Way Home.

title: Iron Man 3
note: Tony deals with PTSD after New York. The Mandarin twist introduces Trevor Slattery.

links.text: Trevor returns, now held by the real Ten Rings.
Trevor is a lead character in Wonder Man.

title: Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King
releaseNote: Released later, on Feb 4, 2014, on the Thor: The Dark World home video.
note: Trevor Slattery in prison, after the events of Iron Man 3.

links.text: Its Ten Rings thread pays off seven years later.

title: The Wolverine
note: Logan travels to Japan.

title: Marvel’s Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
note: Phil Coulson’s team keeps working after The Avengers, with loose ties to the films.

links.text: The first season turns on the fall of S.H.I.E.L.D. in The Winter Soldier.
Clark Gregg’s Coulson appears in Captain Marvel.

title: Thor: The Dark World
note: Thor and Jane face the dark elves over the Aether. Mid-credits scene: {{the Aether is revealed as an Infinity Stone and handed to the Collector.}}

links.text: The Collector scene links the stone storyline to the cosmic side.

title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
note: Cap goes on the run. {{S.H.I.E.L.D. falls to Hydra and Bucky is revealed as the Winter Soldier.}} Mid-credits scene: {{Wanda and Pietro appear.}}

links.text: Wanda and Pietro return.
Bucky’s trauma and Sam’s friendship drive the series.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
note: Peter faces Electro and the Green Goblin.

links.text: Jamie Foxx’s Electro returns in No Way Home.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
note: Wolverine is sent back to the 1970s, bringing the original and First Class casts together.

links.text: Evan Peters’s Fox-era Quicksilver appears in WandaVision.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy
note: A thief, an assassin, a raccoon, a tree and a brute fight over an Infinity Stone. {{Thanos is introduced as the force behind Ronan.}}

links.text: The same team gets a sequel.

title: Marvel’s Agent Carter
note: Peggy Carter works for the Strategic Scientific Reserve in the late 1940s.

links.text: Peggy’s story continues after the war.

title: Marvel’s Daredevil
note: Matt Murdock vs. Wilson Fisk in Hell’s Kitchen. Season 2 introduces Frank Castle (the Punisher) and Elektra, and brings in the Hand.

links.text: Vincent D’Onofrio’s Fisk appears in Hawkeye.
Frank Castle’s debut leads to his own series.

title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
note: Ultron is born. {{Vision is built around the Mind Stone, and Wanda joins the Avengers.}}

links.text: Wanda and Vision’s relationship starts here.
Ultron and Vision’s origins loom over VisionQuest.

title: Ant-Man
note: Scott Lang inherits the suit from Hank Pym. {{Falcon cameos.}}

links.text: Scott joins Cap’s side.
Hope and Hank’s story continues.

title: Marvel’s Jessica Jones
note: Jessica Jones, a private investigator with super strength, is hunted by Kilgrave.

title: Deadpool
note: Wade Wilson’s origin and revenge, in Fox’s R-rated X-Men spinoff.

links.text: Ryan Reynolds’s Deadpool crosses into the MCU in Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Captain America: Civil War
note: The Avengers split over the Sokovia Accords. Black Panther and Tom Holland’s Spider-Man debut. {{Zemo plays the long game.}}

links.text: T’Challa gets his own film.
Peter’s debut leads into Homecoming.
The Accords, Zemo and Bucky’s fallout return.

title: Team Thor
releaseNote: Released later, on Sep 13, 2016, on the Civil War home video.
note: Taika Waititi’s mockumentary short about Thor’s life in Australia with his roommate Darryl. Played for laughs, and left out of Disney+’s main timeline when it was added.

links.text: It covers where Thor was during Civil War.

title: Team Thor: Part 2
releaseNote: Released later, on Feb 14, 2017, on the Doctor Strange home video.
note: The Darryl mockumentary continues, before Ragnarok.

title: X-Men: Apocalypse
note: The first mutant, Apocalypse, wakes up in 1983.

title: Marvel’s Luke Cage
note: A bulletproof man protects Harlem. No MCU appearance yet.

title: Doctor Strange
note: Stephen Strange learns magic. {{He takes the Time Stone, and Mordo walks away from sorcerers.}}

links.text: Strange’s multiverse story continues.
Strange’s spellcasting returns in No Way Home.

title: Logan
note: An older Logan and a young mutant on the run, in Hugh Jackman’s last Wolverine film of that era.

links.text: Logan’s story is referenced in Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Marvel’s Iron Fist
note: Danny Rand returns to New York with kung fu powers. No MCU appearance yet.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
note: Peter meets his father, Ego. Credits scenes: {{Ravagers and Adam Warlock show up.}}

links.text: Adam Warlock and the Ravagers pay off.

title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
note: Peter Parker vs. Adrian Toomes. Establishes the Department of Damage Control.

links.text: Damage Control returns in Wonder Man.

title: Marvel’s The Defenders
note: Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist team up against the Hand.

title: Marvel’s Inhumans
note: The royal family of Attilan, led by Black Bolt, lands in Hawaii. Loosely connected to the Inhumans in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

links.text: Both shows use the Inhumans, but they stay separate stories.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
note: Thor loses Mjolnir and teams up with Hulk and Valkyrie. Mid-credits scene: {{Thanos’s ship arrives.}}

links.text: Valkyrie and New Asgard continue.
Thanos’s ship leads straight into Infinity War.

title: Team Darryl
releaseNote: Released later, on Feb 20, 2018, on the Thor: Ragnarok home video.
note: Thor has moved out. {{Darryl’s new roommate is Jeff Goldblum’s Grandmaster.}}

title: Marvel’s The Punisher
note: Jon Bernthal’s Frank Castle gets his own series.

links.text: Bernthal’s Frank returns in Born Again.
Bernthal’s Frank gets One Last Kill.

title: Black Panther
note: T’Challa becomes king and faces Killmonger. {{Wakanda opens up to the world.}}

links.text: Shuri and Wakanda carry on after T’Challa.
Wakanda’s hidden history is expanded.

title: Marvel’s Jessica Jones
note: Jessica digs into where her powers came from, and the series wraps up in season 3.

links.text: Krysten Ritter’s Jessica Jones joins Born Again season 2.

title: Avengers: Infinity War
note: Thanos goes after the Infinity Stones. {{He snaps half of all life away.}}

links.text: The Avengers try to undo it.

title: Deadpool 2
note: Deadpool puts together X-Force to protect a young mutant.

links.text: Colossus and Negasonic Teenage Warhead return in Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Marvel’s Cloak & Dagger
note: Two teenagers in New Orleans, Tandy Bowen and Tyrone Johnson, find their powers are linked. No MCU appearance yet.

title: Marvel’s Luke Cage
note: Luke Cage faces Bushmaster.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
note: Introduces Ghost (Ava Starr). Post-credits scene: {{Hank, Hope and Janet are caught by the Snap.}}

links.text: Ghost returns as a Thunderbolts* teammate.
The Quantum Realm becomes Kang’s stage.

title: Marvel’s Iron Fist
note: Danny Rand takes on new threats in New York.

title: Venom
note: Eddie Brock bonds with the Venom symbiote. Part of Sony’s Spider-Man Universe, outside the MCU proper.

title: Marvel’s Daredevil
note: Matt Murdock recovers while Fisk schemes.

links.text: Born Again continues Matt’s story from the Netflix series.
Charlie Cox’s Matt Murdock appears in No Way Home.

title: Captain Marvel
note: Carol Danvers’s origin, the Skrulls and Talos, and a young Monica Rambeau.

links.text: Monica returns as an adult.
Talos and the Skrull refugees return.
Carol and Monica are reunited.

title: Avengers: Endgame
note: The Avengers try to undo the Snap. {{They use time travel, and Cap hands his shield to Sam.}}

links.text: Sam’s decision to take up the shield.
Loki’s escape with the Tesseract creates the TVA story.

title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
note: Peter takes a school trip to Europe, where Mysterio appears. {{Mysterio exposes Peter’s identity, and Fury and Hill are revealed to be Skrulls.}}

links.text: The Skrull Fury story continues.
Peter’s outing sets up No Way Home.

title: WandaVision
note: Wanda and Vision appear to live inside a sitcom. {{Wanda’s grief builds the reality.}} Introduces Agatha Harkness, adult Monica Rambeau and {{White Vision}}.

links.text: Wanda’s turn as the Scarlet Witch and the Darkhold.
Agatha gets her own series.
Monica’s powers feed into The Marvels.
White Vision’s fate is picked up in VisionQuest.

title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
note: {{Sam takes the shield.}} Introduces John Walker (US Agent), Isaiah Bradley and Joaquin Torres, and {{reveals Sharon Carter as the Power Broker.}} End credits: {{Val appears.}}

links.text: Sam as Captain America, plus Isaiah Bradley and Torres.
Bucky, John Walker and Val return in Thunderbolts*.

title: Loki
note: The TVA captures a Loki variant, who teams up with Sylvie. {{The finale reveals He Who Remains, a Kang variant, and opens up the multiverse.}}

links.text: Kang the Conqueror gets his debut film.
Season 2 deals with the fallout.

title: Black Widow
note: Natasha’s family story, with Yelena, Red Guardian and Taskmaster. Post-credits scene: {{Val appears.}}

links.text: Yelena’s grudge against Clint is set up.
Yelena, Red Guardian and Val reunite.

title: What If…?
note: Animated multiverse anthology narrated by the Watcher. Includes “What If… Zombies?!” in episode 5.

links.text: The zombie episode spins off into Marvel Zombies.

title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
note: Shang-Chi vs. his father Wenwu. Trevor Slattery returns. Mid-credits scene: {{Wong, Carol and Bruce appear.}}

links.text: Trevor’s Ten Rings history is referenced.

title: Venom: Let There Be Carnage
note: Eddie and Venom face Carnage. {{A mid-credits scene pulls Eddie toward the MCU.}}

links.text: Eddie’s trip to the MCU ends in No Way Home’s mid-credits scene.

title: Eternals
note: Celestials, Deviants and a team of immortals. Introduces Dane Whitman{{, the future Black Knight}}.

links.text: The Celestial Island rises in Brave New World.

title: Hawkeye
note: Clint trains Kate Bishop. Yelena enters the story, Maya Lopez (Echo) is introduced, and {{the finale brings in Wilson Fisk (Vincent D’Onofrio).}}

links.text: Maya Lopez gets her own series, and Kingpin’s story continues.
Fisk is the mayor in Born Again.

title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
note: A broken spell brings in other Spider-Man villains. {{Matt Murdock appears as Peter’s lawyer, and the world ends up forgetting Peter Parker.}}

links.text: Matt Murdock’s return leads to Born Again.
Peter’s erased identity sets up Brand New Day.

title: Moon Knight
note: Marc Spector, Steven Grant and Khonshu. Largely self-contained{{, with a Jake Lockley tease}}.

title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
note: Strange and America Chavez {{face a Darkhold-corrupted Wanda}}. {{Brings in the Illuminati.}} Mid-credits scene: {{Clea appears.}}

title: Ms. Marvel
note: Kamala Khan discovers her powers. Damage Control appears. {{She learns she’s a mutant, and the final scene has her swapping places with Carol Danvers.}}

links.text: The swap with Carol leads into The Marvels.

title: Thor: Love and Thunder
note: Thor vs. Gorr, and Jane Foster becomes the Mighty Thor.

title: I Am Groot
note: Five animated shorts following Baby Groot.

title: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
note: Jen Walters becomes She-Hulk. {{Abomination returns, Matt Murdock appears as Daredevil, and the finale breaks the fourth wall.}}

links.text: Daredevil’s MCU return leads to Born Again.

title: Werewolf by Night
note: A Special Presentation: monster hunters gather for the Bloodstone. Introduces Elsa Bloodstone and Ted.

title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
note: Wakanda mourns T’Challa, and Namor and Talokan debut. Introduces Riri Williams. {{Shuri becomes Black Panther, and Val appears.}}

links.text: Riri Williams’s debut leads into Ironheart.
Val appears again.

title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
note: Mantis and Drax try to give Peter Quill a Christmas. Kevin Bacon plays himself.

links.text: Sets up the team before Vol. 3.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
note: Scott, Hope and their family are trapped in the Quantum Realm. Kang the Conqueror debuts.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
note: The High Evolutionary and Rocket’s origin. {{The Guardians go their separate ways.}}

title: Secret Invasion
note: Skrull infiltration and Nick Fury’s return to Earth.

links.text: Fury’s space station links to The Marvels.

title: Loki
note: Loki, Mobius and the TVA try to stabilize the timeline. {{Introduces Victor Timely, another Kang variant.}}

links.text: The TVA returns in Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: The Marvels
note: Carol, Monica and Kamala swap places whenever they use their powers. Mid-credits scene: {{Beast (Kelsey Grammer) appears.}}

title: What If…?
note: Season 2 released one episode a day over the holidays.

title: Echo
note: Maya Lopez returns home. The first Marvel Spotlight series, released all at once.

links.text: Maya and Kingpin continue in Born Again.

title: Deadpool & Wolverine
note: Deadpool and Wolverine team up at the TVA. {{Chris Evans cameos as Johnny Storm, and mutants enter the Sacred Timeline.}}

title: Agatha All Along
note: Agatha Harkness regains her powers on the Witches’ Road. Introduces Billy Maximoff.

links.text: The trilogy concludes with VisionQuest.

title: Venom: The Last Dance
note: Eddie and Venom on the run.

title: What If…?
note: The final season, released over the holidays.

title: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man
note: Animated take on Peter Parker’s early days. Season 2 arrives Jan 13, 2027, so it falls outside this chart.

links.text: Doctor Strange’s portal is how the radioactive spider arrives.
Charlie Cox voices Matt Murdock ahead of Born Again.

title: Captain America: Brave New World
note: Sam Wilson as Captain America. {{Ross becomes Red Hulk, Samuel Sterns becomes the Leader, and the Celestial Island appears.}}

title: Daredevil: Born Again
note: Matt Murdock faces Mayor Fisk. The Punisher returns.

links.text: Season 2 continues the fight.
Frank’s escape in the finale leads to One Last Kill.

title: Thunderbolts*
note: Yelena, Bucky, John Walker, Red Guardian, Ghost and Taskmaster {{are manipulated into a team by Val}}. Introduces Bob (Sentry). Post-credits scene: {{the team is shown as the New Avengers.}}

links.text: The Fantastic Four’s ship appears in the post-credits scene.

title: Ironheart
note: Riri Williams returns to Chicago and clashes with Parker Robbins (the Hood) over technology and magic.

title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
note: Marvel’s First Family on Earth-828 face Galactus. Post-credits scene: {{Doom appears.}}

links.text: Doom’s post-credits appearance leads to Doomsday.

title: Eyes of Wakanda
note: Animated miniseries on Wakanda’s hidden history. Marvel moved it earlier from Aug 27.

title: Marvel Zombies
note: Adult animated spinoff of the What If… zombie episode.

title: Wonder Man
note: Simon Williams (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) and Trevor Slattery in Hollywood, where the Doorman Clause bars superpowered actors. A Marvel Spotlight series. {{Damage Control and Agent Cleary appear in the background.}}

title: Daredevil: Born Again
note: Matt builds an army against Fisk, with Krysten Ritter’s Jessica Jones joining. The Punisher sits this season out.

links.text: Marvel says the season ties directly into Brand New Day.
The special covers where Frank is.

title: The Punisher: One Last Kill
note: Jon Bernthal’s one-hour Special Presentation, released one week after the Born Again season 2 finale.

links.text: Frank also appears in Brand New Day.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
note: Peter Parker in a world that doesn’t remember him. {{The Punisher and Hulk appear}}, and the film is set in the New York of Born Again.

title: VisionQuest
note: Paul Bettany returns as White Vision, closing out the WandaVision and Agatha All Along trilogy. Terry Matalas is the showrunner. {{Vision traps Ultron in a sitcom of his own, and Billy and Tommy bring Vision back.}} Post-credits scenes: {{Ultron, now in human form, holds on to Jocasta; then Doom digs Wanda out of the rubble at Wundagore and she opens her eyes.}}

links.text: Doom reviving Wanda leads into Doomsday.
The scene returns to Wundagore right after Wanda’s fall.

title: Avengers: Doomsday
note: Opens about five weeks after VisionQuest’s finale and sits outside the chart.

leadIns.text: its post-credits scene sets up Doom’s role.
its final post-credits scene has Doom reviving Wanda.
